messages:
sam_cs: Quick heads-up — Bluecrest procurement wants to split the renewal invoice across two legal entities (US parent + DE subsidiary) for a 12-seat midterm add. They also want pro‑rata for the remainder of the term and insist on a wet signature for the amendment. Can we confirm feasibility and timing?
priya_am: Noted. We can do pro‑rata. Need exact add date and term end to calc. Also: do they want two invoices or one invoice with allocation lines?
lina_fin: Two separate invoices is easiest for tax purposes. Finance needs vendor codes + VAT ID for DE entity. If PO omits VAT, we'll flag and may delay. Payment terms per entity = net30 unless Procurement says otherwise.
marcus_legal: Wet signature request for DE — is it coming from their legal? Docusign with qualified signature sometimes acceptable but tends to be rejected by some German auditors. If they insist on wet, legal will require: (1) signed amendment PDF, (2) signatory name + title, (3) scanned signature page with attestation clause.
sam_cs: They sent a procurement email referencing "Bluecrest GmbH" but their PO number maps to the parent account in our system. Procurement says they need the vendor code tied to GmbH on PO. They're asking for final invoice by 2024-03-15 to meet quarter close.
priya_am: I'll draft an amendment that supports split billing and proration. @marcus_legal can you confirm a short attestation snippet we can include so their legal team signs once? Also @lina_fin will need the exact numbers to generate two invoices.
lina_fin: For numbers please provide: (a) seats added, (b) add effective date, (c) original term end date, (d) per-seat rate. Formula: ```prorated_amount = seats * seat_rate * (remaining_days / total_term_days)``` We'll need separate calculations per entity if they split seats between entities.
priya_am: Customer wants all 12 seats on the DE entity for the remainder but split historical billing to parent for the prior balance. So only the midterm add invoices to DE. Effective add date = 2024-02-20, term end = 2025-02-19. Seat rate = 1200 USD/seat/yr (same as committed).
marcus_legal: Ok — amendment language: "Customer confirms authorized signatory with wet signature; scanned signature page shall constitute binding execution for the purposes of this amendment." I can paste final clause once draft looks right.
sam_cs: Procurement also attached a PO draft that uses old legal name and missing VAT. They've asked us to re-issue the PO mapping table before signing. Can we produce a one-page mapping they can attach?
priya_am: Yes, I'll include a mapping table in the amendment doc and send to Solutions to review. Timeline: I can send first draft by EOD today. Can Legal review within 24 hours?
marcus_legal: 24h review ok. If they insist on wet signature we'll need a scanned PDF from authorized signatory; we can accept via email and attach to agreement.
lina_fin: Assuming we get PO + VAT by 3/12 and signed amendment by 3/14, finance can issue DE invoice by 3/15. Any delay in PO/VAT or signatory confirmation pushes timeline.
docu_sign_bot: DocuSign envelope prepared (env_id: 0a9f-bleu-1234) — placeholder for amendment. Will switch to "wet signature required" workflow if Legal flags it. :gear:
sam_cs: Thanks team. I'll coordinate with the customer: ask them to (1) confirm VAT ID + vendor code for Bluecrest GmbH, (2) provide scanned signatory if wet required, (3) approve mapping table. I'll post draft amendment when @priya_am attaches it. :thumbsup:
priya_am: Draft uploaded: https://redwood.docs/amendments/BR-2024-midterm-draft.pdf — please review. Marcus, Lina — pinging for rapid review.
marcus_legal: Reviewing now. If clean I'll add signature attestation and return by 3/11 EOD.
lina_fin: I'll prepare invoice templates for both entities and share with Priya after Legal confirms language.
sam_cs: Perfect — I'll keep Bluecrest updated. If procurement escalates, I'll route to Sales Ops.
priya_am: Noted. Will update thread after legal + finance confirm.
docu_sign_bot: Status update: envelope 0a9f-bleu-1234 set to "manual upload (wet-sign)" per legal request.
priya_am: Final note — if they insist on a physical courier to collect wet signature, we should avoid unless their legal truly requires; scanned signed PDF is typically sufficient. I'll call the procurement lead now. :phone:
